title: Traveling Waves & Sound as a Pressure Wave
theory: $v = f\lambda$, $f = 1/T$. There are **two graph types — never mix them**: a graph vs. **time** at fixed position reveals the period $T$; a **snapshot** vs. position at fixed time reveals the wavelength $\lambda$. Sound is a longitudinal *pressure* wave: **maximum density ⇔ maximum pressure** (peak of $\Delta P$). The displacement wave is 90° out of phase with the pressure wave — a pressure antinode is a displacement node.

formulas.description: Pressure amplitude = peak of the — axis
peak→adjacent trough = half a period (or half a wavelength)

framework: Density questions → the $\Delta P$ curve, not the displacement curve.

problems.title: Sound wave read from a ΔP–t graph and a snapshot (parts 1–4)

parts.title: Amplitude of the pressure variation
parts.parameters:
- Given: sound travels toward $+x$ at speed $v$; at a fixed point, $\Delta P(t)$ is sinusoidal with maximum $+A$ at $t_1$ and the next minimum $-A$ at $t_2$; a later $\Delta P(x)$ snapshot marks axis points a, b, c, d, with the curve at its maximum at d.
- Find: pressure amplitude; period; wavelength; the highest-density point on the snapshot.
parts.calculations: peak value of the curve $= A$.

parts.title: Period
parts.parameters:
- Given: sound travels toward $+x$ at speed $v$; at a fixed point, $\Delta P(t)$ is sinusoidal with maximum $+A$ at $t_1$ and the next minimum $-A$ at $t_2$; a later $\Delta P(x)$ snapshot marks axis points a, b, c, d, with the curve at its maximum at d.
- Find: pressure amplitude; period; wavelength; the highest-density point on the snapshot.
parts.formulas: maximum → next minimum spans **half** a cycle.

parts.title: Wavelength
parts.parameters:
- Given: sound travels toward $+x$ at speed $v$; at a fixed point, $\Delta P(t)$ is sinusoidal with maximum $+A$ at $t_1$ and the next minimum $-A$ at $t_2$; a later $\Delta P(x)$ snapshot marks axis points a, b, c, d, with the curve at its maximum at d.
- Find: pressure amplitude; period; wavelength; the highest-density point on the snapshot.
parts.conclusion: (2)→(3) chain — a period error doubles through. Always re-derive (2) before trusting (3).

parts.title: Point of highest air density
parts.parameters:
- Given: sound travels toward $+x$ at speed $v$; at a fixed point, $\Delta P(t)$ is sinusoidal with maximum $+A$ at $t_1$ and the next minimum $-A$ at $t_2$; a later $\Delta P(x)$ snapshot marks axis points a, b, c, d, with the curve at its maximum at d.
- Find: pressure amplitude; period; wavelength; the highest-density point on the snapshot.
parts.formulas: highest density ⇔ maximum $\Delta P$ on the snapshot.
parts.calculations: the curve peaks at point d.
parts.conclusion: compressions live at pressure **maxima**. If a year instead shows the *displacement* snapshot, the compression sits where displacement crosses zero with negative slope (for $+x$ travel) — know both pictures so neither version surprises you.
